title: Add Passkey (WebAuthn) Authentication to Existing NestJS Auth Flow
summary: Extend the existing authentication module to support passwordless login and registration using passkeys (WebAuthn standard) alongside existing email/password authentication.

context.current_state: Has working user registration, login, and session or JWT auth.
context.new_feature_goal: Enable users to register and log in with passkeys as an alternative to password auth, while maintaining compatibility with the existing system.

database_changes.description: Stores registered WebAuthn credentials tied to users.

endpoints.description: Generates WebAuthn registration (credential creation) options for the logged-in user.
Verifies the credential response from the client and stores the new public key credential.
Generates WebAuthn authentication (assertion) options for known credentials.
Verifies a passkey-based login attempt and issues a JWT session token.

registration_flow: 2. Store challenge temporarily in Redis or in-memory keyed by user id.
4. On verify, call verifyRegistrationResponse() with stored challenge and expected RP_ID/Origin.
5. If verified, extract publicKey, credentialId, signCount, store in credentials table linked to user.
authentication_flow: 1. Lookup user’s credentials by email or user id.
3. Store challenge keyed by user id.
5. If verified, update signCount and issue JWT or session cookie.

frontend_integration.description: Frontend should use WebAuthn APIs in browser to create and get credentials.

files.purpose: Handles navigator.credentials.create() and navigator.credentials.get() calls with server endpoints.

example_code_snippets.service: Use @simplewebauthn/server to handle generateRegistrationOptions(), verifyRegistrationResponse(), generateAuthenticationOptions(), verifyAuthenticationResponse()
example_code_snippets.controller: Expose 4 endpoints mapped to the methods in WebauthnService
example_code_snippets.entity: Define Credential entity matching the database schema
example_code_snippets.integration: After verification, login flow should issue JWT via existing AuthService

testing.integration_tests: Simulate full registration and authentication flows

readme_tasks: Document new endpoints and frontend calls.
Explain how to test locally using HTTPS (localhost with mkcert).
Describe optional Redis setup for challenge caching.
expected_output: Working passkey authentication integrated with existing NestJS AuthModule, supporting both password and passkey login flows.
